display.purpose: Hero nameplate and section titles only. WONK axis on for character.

body.purpose: All prose; capped to the 760px reading column for long-form sections.

label.purpose: Publication chrome only: masthead, dates, kickers, metadata.

signature.purpose: Reserved for the nav 'AP' mark and the Contact sign-off only.

shadows.name: photo-frame-lift
shadows.purpose: Soft ambient lift under real framed photographs only.

shadows.name: status-pip-halo
shadows.purpose: Living-status signal on the masthead pip and the current-role timeline dot; pulses to a wider, fainter ring.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard-only focus indicator via :focus-visible; never shown on mouse interaction.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition easing across nav, links, and hover states (0.2-0.4s durations).

motion.name: reduced-motion-fallback
motion.purpose: Honored three ways: CSS media query, framer MotionConfig reducedMotion='user', and manual guards in canvas components (hero particles, globe autorotate).

components.name: Text-Link CTA
components.description: Primary call to action, phrased as a sentence fragment, never a boxed button.
components.html: Read the full case study →
components.css: .ds-cta { color: #bca47a; font-family: 'Newsreader', Georgia, serif; font-style: italic; font-size: 1rem; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.2s; } .ds-cta:hover { color: #d3c09e; } .ds-cta:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #bca47a; outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Section Header
components.description: The load-bearing triad opening every section: hairline rule, Fraunces title, italic Newsreader subtitle.
components.html:
Projects

Selected work, in brief.
components.css: .ds-section-header { position: relative; padding-top: 20px; } .ds-section-header::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 36px; height: 1px; background: #bca47a; } .ds-section-title { font-family: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; font-variation-settings: 'opsz' 144, 'WONK' 1; font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 4vw, 3rem); color: #f0e2c5; } .ds-section-subtitle { font-family: 'Newsreader', Georgia, serif; font-style: italic; color: #d6c9ad; margin-top: 6px; }

components.name: Status Pip
components.description: Pulsing circular status indicator (masthead 'open to roles', Leadership current-role dot).
components.css: .ds-status-pip { display: inline-block; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: #bca47a; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(188,164,122,0.18); animation: ds-pulse 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(188,164,122,0.18); } 50% { opacity: 0.55; box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px rgba(188,164,122,0.05); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-status-pip { animation: none; } }

components.name: Mono Tag
components.description: Hashtag-style research tag; mono-caps pill, used sparingly.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 20px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.03em; color: #8a9d84; border: 1px solid rgba(125,144,121,0.3); }

components.name: Photo Frame
components.description: Framed photograph treatment used in Highlights and About inline figures; the only element carrying a default shadow.
components.css: .ds-photo-frame { box-shadow: 0 6px 14px rgba(0,0,0,0.28); border-radius: 2px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-photo-caption { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; color: #b3a48c; margin-top: 8px; }

narrative.overview: The site presents itself as a personal magazine: a running publication with a masthead, section entries that read as articles rather than app screens, and a single sign-off voice at the close. The paper is warm cardstock, not stark white or SaaS-black; ink is cream, not pure white, so nothing on the page reads as a display panel. A restrained WebGL hero and a holographic globe supply the one moment of technical spectacle the rest of the page earns the right to have, by keeping everything else quiet.
keyCharacteristics: One voice color (oat) does all the 'look here' work; sage and ink-blue are rare, calm seconds.
Long-form prose treatment wherever content is genuinely long-read (drop caps, pull quotes, 760px column).
Baked paper-grain texture plus a warm-sepia wash, fixed and pointer-events-none.
Hairline rules and the ⁂ asterism do the separating work instead of borders and shadows.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Oat is the only color allowed to signal 'pay attention here.' A second element needing emphasis competes with the first; redesign the hierarchy instead of adding a second accent.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the system is true black or true white. Every surface and ink value carries the same warm cardstock/cream undertone.

rules.name: The Three-Family Ceiling
rules.body: Fraunces + Newsreader + IBM Plex Mono is the working system. Caveat is a fourth, capped to two specific signature moments.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow only lifts a real photograph or signals a live status, never generic card chrome.

dos: Do let oat carry every 'pay attention' moment; keep sage and ink-blue rare and calm.
Do phrase CTAs as text links in a sentence, not boxed buttons.
Do use hairline rules and the ⁂ asterism to separate sections instead of shadows or card borders.
Do keep the reading column at 760px for long-form prose sections.
Do carry the section-header triad (rule + Fraunces title + italic subtitle) on every new section.
donts: Don't introduce gradient-clipped headline text anywhere in the system.
Don't add a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow above a section as generic scaffolding.
Don't build identical icon+heading+text card grids; Projects and Research are articles, not cards.
Don't reach for a second saturated accent color for emphasis.
Don't add default card-shadow chrome; shadows are reserved for real photographs and live-status pips only.
Don't use pure black or pure white anywhere.
Don't use emoji as structural icons; all icons are inline SVG from src/icons.jsx.
